title: Rabbi Yirmiya bar Abba (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He too was a Babylonian, a student of Rav Huna, as is explicit in Kiddushin 46a, where Rav Huna and Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba disagree there — Ulla said: this statement of Rav Huna is like vinegar to the teeth — the words of the student appear [correct]. And he went up to the Land of Israel even before Rabbi Zeira went up, as in Chullin 76b: when Rabbi Zeira went up he found Rabbi Yirmiyah [bar Abba, Rashi] sitting and saying it — he said to him: well done. And he received [teachings] from Rabbi Yohanan, as we find in Ketubot 111a, Niddah 23b, Tanchuma Bamidbar 27: Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said Rabbi Yohanan; and Berakhot 39b, the dispute of Rav Huna and Rabbi Yohanan, and regarding this Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said it is [a dispute] of tannaim.
And in Taanit 11b, Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba [reports a teaching] said by Resh Lakish.
And in Chullin 57a, Rabbi Abba found Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba examining the juncture of the sinews; he said to him: why does the master need all this — did not Rav Huna say in the name of Rav, etc.
And in Tanchuma Bamidbar 27, Rabbi Hizkiah said in his name.
And in the Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubot ch. 1, halakhah 10, he disagrees with Rabbi Yosi, whom Hyman identifies as Rabbi Assi.

notes.text: Hyman identifies the Yerushalmi Rabbi Yosi with Rabbi Assi; the pronoun does not identify Yirmiya with Assi.

The inspected dispute begins in Kiddushin 45b and continues with “the student’s words appear” at 46a, Hyman’s supplied folio. It directly names Huna and Yirmiyah bar Abba and the vinegar-to-teeth comparison. Rashi’s bracketed name expansion elsewhere and Hyman’s migration and Yosi/Assi identification remain attributed.
